Ah, thanks for clarifying. A few differences:

Guilded is specifically for gaming, so the tools are more powerful for gamers and tailored for gaming content. For instance, if you're a WoW player, you can filter to teams/players on your server, in your faction, with a certain class, and with a certain ilvl. Facebook doesn't have similar recruiting tools. Facebook also doesn't allow you to integrate with your gaming accounts - on Guilded, for example, you can link your Xbox LIVE account and share your game clips with your teammates, or link your Twitch account and have your Twitch videos on your profile.

Twitch is awesome for gamers, I think it's complementary. Twitch is great for streaming, but not great for managing a team calendar (think raids, matches, etc.), long-form discussions/docs, etc. Twitch also lacks the recruiting tools I described above, and more advanced chat features like team chat.

The idea behind Guilded is that it's a single place to do what Twitch, Steam, etc. aren't good at - more advanced team management, recruiting, and integration with your gaming profiles. This is usually most useful for competitive/serious teams.
